summary: Iteration 7: tested the automatic order list and recipe-cost features on the backend and frontend. Backend: 9 of 9 pytest tests passed. 5 are new for iteration 7 and 4 are iteration-6 regression tests. Frontend: the full UI flow passed. It created ingredients with target, unit_cost and supplier in the modal, checked the order list grouping and amounts, the WhatsApp links and copy-to-clipboard, built a product with a recipe, checked the auto cost with the 'tariften' badge and per-ingredient costs, recorded a sale that dropped stock below minimum, and checked the order list update, report profit, recompute after a unit_cost edit, stock movements and the custom-range calendar.

minor.issue: The backend takes unit_cost from the client payload and does not read it from product.cost. A sale posted without unit_cost is stored with unit_cost=0, so profit is overstated. The frontend always sends product.cost, so the UI is not affected.

An item with minimum=0 and quantity=0 is listed with suggested=0, because the check is 0<=0. If target is lower than the current quantity, the item is also listed with suggested 0. Consider leaving out items whose suggested amount is 0.
When the recipe is removed from a product, the old recipe-derived cost is kept as the manual cost, since the frontend form still holds it. This may be acceptable, but nothing tells the user.

issues: Recipe amounts use dot decimals ('0.1 kg') while the rest of the UI uses tr-TR formatting ('0,1').
Per-item estimated cost is not shown, only the group total.
There is an empty gap between the group header and the first item in single-item groups.

action_items: Optional: on sale create/update, have the backend set unit_cost from product.cost when it is missing or 0.
Optional: leave items with suggested == 0 out of the order list.
Optional: format recipe amounts with tr-TR in ProductView.
critical_code_review_comments: recompute_product_costs runs on every inventory POST/PUT/DELETE, including quantity-only edits. It does one update per product (N writes). This is fine at this scale, but it could be limited to unit_cost changes.
Sale cost is a snapshot at sale time. This is correct, but past report profit does not change when an ingredient price changes. That is expected and could be documented for the user.
Empty state ('Sipariş gereken malzeme yok') was checked by code review only, because non-test data with critical stock exists in the DB.
seed_data_creation: None. Every TEST_ record created was deleted by id (sales, products, inventory), along with their stock_movements. report_deliveries and cron_runs were already 0. The DB was NOT empty at the start: non-test records Domates, Dana kıyma (inventory) and Köfte (product), plus 2 stock_movements, created at 14:24 by someone else. They were left untouched.
